invariants: No write may resolve onto a raw partition block device, a BOOT/USERDATA/SYSTEM/RECOVERY/DTB/DTBO/VBMETA image, the radio/modem, EFS/SEC_EFS/calibration/IMEI/PIT or any partition metadata.
No Heimdall/Odin/wrapper, no Download Mode, no TWRP, no new kernel on the phone.
Every deploy target must live under an allowed userspace root (assert_userspace_path).
Recovery/Download-Mode power-menu entries may be implemented and offline-tested but are never triggered by this group.
Stage -> verify SHA-256 -> atomic install -> restart the smallest affected service -> health check -> automatic rollback on failure.

Every group declares a risk class (low|medium|high), a component, a health_check, rollback text, and EITHER a restart_service OR a deliberate reload (declared_reload, or a group_reload_notes entry for a byte-frozen core group). validate_manifest() refuses the plan otherwise, before any device contact.

Sources must resolve INSIDE this repository (no absolute path, no `..`): nothing is staged from the host filesystem, and a source the repository does not carry is refused rather than silently dropped.

Nothing may be staged from a gitignored build directory: a compiled artefact is either a tracked file or it is produced by a documented install procedure with its own verdict (INSTALL_PROCEDURE_REQUIRED).
The extension block is authored in ASCENDING RISK order (low -> medium -> high) with non-decreasing priority; validate_manifest() refuses a backwards step.

Targets are confined to userspace roots by assert_userspace_path(); no target can resolve onto a raw partition, an .img, a DTB/DTBO, the modem/EFS/PIT calibration region or the BOOT container. The extension block makes the remainder of the built programme deployable under the same stage->verify->install->restart->health->rollback discipline, and names everything deliberately NOT deployable in non_deployable[] with a reason and a terminal state.

Every target authored under /home/nuxel/nuxel is remapped here before it is guarded, planned or executed, so a deploy actually changes what the running phone reads.
